answer: The RNA expression distribution is HIGHLY RIGHT-SKEWED. Pooled over all 6,724,656 gene-by-sample values in data/COAD__geneExp.xls (20,502 genes x 328 TCGA-COAD samples, linear normalized scale, 15.24% exact zeros), the sample skewness coefficient (scipy.stats.skew, bias=True) is g1 = +42.44 (mean 932.0 vs median 176.8; max 1,336,107). Sensitivity checks: raw scale with zeros excluded g1 = +39.55; log1p-transformed values g1 = -0.30 (slightly left-skewed), showing the extreme right skew is driven by a heavy tail of very high expression values plus a large zero/low-expression mass. Secondary observation: on the log1p scale the distribution is only slightly left-skewed, not normal.
